also: why is everyone picking on me?

terms.gloss: pick at, carp at, find fault with
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, transitive: aliquem carpere
evidence: Cic. Q. fr. 2.3.2: is carpēbātur ā Bibulō, Curiōne, Favōniō (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Balb. 57: maledicō dente carpunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The same verb as “pluck, pick” (fruit, flowers): Lewis & Short, “to gnaw at or tear character or reputation, to carp at”.

phrases.latin: Cūr omnēs in hāc familiā mē carpunt?
phrases.english: Why does everyone in this family pick on me?

sources: Lewis & Short: carpo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 36, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
